question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&a&4\\0&0&b\end{pmatrix}$, show that $|A| = ab$.
explanation:
$A$ is upper triangular.

Determinant is product of diagonal entries:

$|A| = 1\cdot a \cdot b = ab$.

options.B: $A$ is upper triangular, so $|A|$ is the sum of diagonal entries, hence $|A|=1+a+b$.
options.C: $A$ is upper triangular, so its determinant is the product of diagonal entries: $|A|=1\cdot a\cdot b=ab$.
options.D: $A$ has two zero entries, so its determinant is always $0$.
